questions.source: SEC Sample Paper 1 (2027), Higher Level, Question 1 (d) (iii), (iv)
questions.stem: The hormone insulin stimulates the uptake of glucose from the bloodstream into cells, particularly in muscles. Glucagon is another hormone that converts stored glycogen back into glucose when needed. Glucose and glycogen are types of carbohydrate. The graph shows a person’s relative blood glucose concentration over a period of time. The person begins eating at the 20 minute mark. Analyse the data and answer the questions that follow.

diagram.what: Line graph 'Blood glucose levels after a meal': relative blood glucose concentration against time, 0-100 minutes. The line is level until about 25 minutes, rises to a peak at about 45 minutes, falls below its starting level to a low at about 90 minutes and starts to rise again by 100.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text: On the horizontal axis above, indicate a time with the letter X, when the secretion of the hormone insulin is likely to start increasing.

points.answer: X marked on the time axis shortly after 20 minutes, where the blood glucose concentration begins to rise after eating
accept: Any point from about 20 to 30 minutes

parts.scheme_note: SimpleStudy practice marking scheme (not an official SEC scheme). (i) and (ii), on carbohydrates, are in another chapter.

parts.label: (iv)
parts.text: Low blood glucose concentration is a stimulus for the secretion of glucagon. On the horizontal axis above, indicate a time with the letter Y, when the secretion of the hormone glucagon is likely to start increasing.

points.answer: Y marked on the time axis late in the trace, where the blood glucose concentration has fallen back to or below the resting level, about 80 to 100 minutes; Y must be later than X

parts.scheme_note: SimpleStudy practice marking scheme (not an official SEC scheme).

not_covered: The parathyroid glands and parathyroid hormone (their place on the thyroid, the hormone raising blood calcium): never asked (2.4.10).
TSH, oxytocin and the other pituitary hormones as hormones of the pituitary: only accepted answers (2019 Q14 (a)(v)); oxytocin is asked only in birth questions (reproduction).
Hormonal manipulation in sport (anabolic steroids, EPO, testosterone doping): never asked (2.4.11).
Hormonal manipulation in agriculture (growth hormones in livestock, hormones to time breeding): never asked (2.4.11).
Blood glucose kept steady by insulin and glucagon as a negative feedback loop (receptor, control centre, response): only the timing on a graph in SEC Sample Paper 1 Q1 (d) (2.4.5).
Homeostasis as a model of stimulus and response with a control centre, receptors and effectors, for a hormonal pathway: asked only as feedback between hormones (2.4.5).
